title: Chicago must be honest about taxes, spending

statements.summary: Opposes raising property taxes, calling it a 'slow poison' and 'surrender'.
statements.quote: City Hall’s latest flirtation with tax hikes, brought to light in Crain’s July 25 editorial, is more than just political posturing — it’s a red flag for every homeowner and business operator in this city.

statements.summary: Supports cutting spending, including layoffs, agency cuts, and program trims, as an alternative to tax hikes.
statements.quote: If the mayor is ruling out property tax hikes, then layoffs, agency cuts, and program trims must be openly discussed.

statements.summary: Supports fixing systemic issues like bloated contracts, opaque work rules, and unchecked overtime to avoid property tax hikes.
statements.quote: If we don’t fix these systemic issues, property tax hikes will become the default solution.

statements.summary: Supports growing the tax base through real projects, bringing back cranes downtown, and reigniting manufacturing.
statements.quote: We need to grow the base — build real projects, bring back cranes downtown, reignite manufacturing on the South and West sides, and capture new value instead of recycling old pain.

statements.summary: Supports streamlining permitting to make the city investment-worthy.
statements.quote: That means streamlining permitting. Eliminating redundancies.

statements.summary: Supports fixing broken property assessments that scare off capital.
statements.quote: Fixing the broken assessments that scare off capital.

statements.summary: Supports moving toward income-based relief mechanisms like the circuit breaker for property tax equity.
statements.quote: There must be equity, and that means moving toward income-based relief mechanisms like the circuit breaker.
